page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-48GB is a Cloud Native family virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared x86_64 vCPUs mapped to physical AMD EPYC 7542 cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with a single complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core execution. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is categorized in the bottom 10% with a score of 787.49, reflecting the shared nature of the CPU allocation. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 12555.22 and Geekbench multi-core score of 8794.0, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is stable, with read-only large block transfers reaching 82.52 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 39.0 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this server is the shared CPU allocation, which limits single-threaded performance but offers a cost-effective resource density for multi-threaded workloads. It achieves average throughput in database operations with 9983.1 on PassMark and static web serving at 11.83 GB/sec. This configuration is appropriate for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and basic web serving where sustained peak single-core performance is not critical.
